boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain Berry College
boards.description: Berry College's massive campus and residential focus mean late-night runs often lead to Rome's reliable 24-hour staples and student-favorite drive-thrus.

cards.title: Waffle House on Martha Berry
cards.subtitle: The 24/7 Campus Neighbor
cards.notes: Located just outside the main gate, this 24-hour diner is the primary destination for late-night breakfast and study breaks.
cards.short_summary: A 24-hour diner located immediately adjacent to the Berry College campus entrance.
cards.evidence_claim: Waffle House #970 at 2903 Martha Berry Hwy is open 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.
cards.access_notes: Open 24 hours daily for dine-in and takeout.

cards.title: Cook Out Trays
cards.subtitle: Late-Night Milkshake Runs
cards.notes: Famous for its extensive milkshake menu and affordable trays, this spot stays open until 2 AM for late-night cravings.
cards.short_summary: A popular regional fast-food chain known for low-cost 'trays' and 40+ milkshake flavors.
cards.evidence_claim: The Cook Out at 808 Martha Berry Blvd NE is open until 2:00 AM daily.
cards.access_notes: Drive-thru and walk-up window open until 2:00 AM.

cards.title: Taco Bell Drive-Thru
cards.subtitle: The 2 AM Fourth Meal
cards.notes: A convenient stop on Martha Berry Highway for students returning to campus late after events in Rome.
cards.short_summary: A fast-food staple located on the main corridor leading to the Berry College campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The Taco Bell at 2837 Martha Berry Highway NW is open until 2:00 AM daily.
cards.source_title: Taco Bell Rome, GA - 2837 Martha Berry Highway NW
cards.access_notes: Drive-thru open until 2:00 AM; lobby hours vary.

cards.title: IHOP on Riverbend
cards.subtitle: 24-Hour Pancake Sessions
cards.notes: A reliable 24-hour alternative for large groups seeking a sit-down meal during finals week or late weekends.
cards.short_summary: A 24-hour breakfast and diner chain located near the Turner McCall corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: The IHOP at 35 Riverbend Dr SW in Rome is open 24 hours a day.
cards.access_notes: Open 24 hours daily for dine-in and takeout.

cards.title: Krystal Sliders
cards.subtitle: Late-Night Southern Classic
cards.notes: Known for its small square burgers, this location serves as a late-night destination for students until 2 AM.
cards.short_summary: A Southern fast-food chain specializing in small sliders and late-night service.
cards.evidence_claim: The Krystal at 519 Shorter Avenue is open until 2:00 AM Monday through Thursday.
cards.access_notes: Open until 2:00 AM most nights; check for weekend variations.

cards.title: Steak 'n Shake
cards.subtitle: Midnight Shakes and Fries
cards.notes: A popular spot for milkshakes and burgers, offering extended hours on Friday and Saturday nights.
cards.short_summary: A classic diner-style chain known for steakburgers and hand-scooped milkshakes.
cards.evidence_claim: The Steak 'n Shake at 838 Turner McCall Blvd SW is open until 12:00 AM on Fridays and Saturdays.
cards.access_notes: Open until 12:00 AM on Friday and Saturday; 10:00 PM other nights.

cards.title: Applebee's Late Night
cards.subtitle: Half-Price Appetizers
cards.notes: A frequent choice for students looking for a sit-down meal and late-night appetizer specials until midnight.
cards.short_summary: A casual dining restaurant offering a full menu and late-night hours in central Rome.
cards.evidence_claim: The Applebee's at 826 Turner McCall Blvd is open until 12:00 AM daily.
cards.access_notes: Open until 12:00 AM daily for dine-in and carside pickup.

cards.title: Mellow Mushroom Pizza
cards.subtitle: Weekend Pizza Runs
cards.notes: Located in downtown Rome, this pizza spot is a favorite for weekend dinners and stays open until 11 PM.
cards.short_summary: An eclectic pizza chain located in the historic Broad Street district of Rome.
cards.evidence_claim: Mellow Mushroom Rome is open until 11:00 PM on Fridays and Saturdays.
cards.access_notes: Open until 11:00 PM on Friday and Saturday; 10:00 PM on Thursday and Sunday.

cards.title: Zaxby's Chicken
cards.subtitle: Post-Event Chicken Runs
cards.notes: A go-to for chicken fingers and wings, conveniently located on the main road back to the Berry campus.
cards.short_summary: A popular Southern chicken chain located near the Berry College campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The Zaxby's at 2790 Martha Berry Hwy NE is open until 10:00 PM daily.
cards.access_notes: Open until 10:00 PM daily for drive-thru and dine-in.

cards.title: Viking Court
cards.subtitle: On-Campus Late Dining
cards.notes: The primary on-campus late-night dining option located in the Krannert Center, serving students until 11 PM.
cards.short_summary: The food court located within the Krannert Student Center on the Berry College campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Viking Court in the Krannert Center offers dining options with hours extending to 11:00 PM on weeknights.
cards.access_notes: Open until 11:00 PM Monday-Thursday; weekend hours vary.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Discover the student-preferred study spots, quiet retreats, and recreational hubs across Berry College's expansive 27,000-acre campus.

cards.title: Social Studying at 'Club Lib'
cards.subtitle: Informal student nickname for the central library
cards.notes: Students refer to the library as 'Club Lib' because it serves as a primary social hub where group studying and socializing happen simultaneously.
cards.short_summary: The central library is a social and academic hub known to students as 'Club Lib'.
cards.evidence_claim: Students actually call it 'Club Lib' as in 'Club Library' because they're studying as well as socializing.
cards.source_title: 23 Berry College Campus Highlights Students Can Get Excited About
cards.access_notes: Open to the Berry community; community guests are welcome to use selected resources upon request.

cards.title: The Mountain-Top Retreat
cards.subtitle: Historic stone cottage on Lavender Mountain
cards.notes: Built by students in 1922, this retreat is used for 'dreaming' sessions and offers views of Georgia, Tennessee, and Alabama.
cards.short_summary: A historic mountain-top cottage built by students for reflection and group meetings.
cards.evidence_claim: It is still used for meetings and 'dreaming' sessions by faculty, staff and student groups.
cards.access_notes: Accessible via a 4.8-mile round-trip hike; visitors must check in at the front gate.

cards.title: Krannert Center Study Nook
cards.subtitle: Quiet lounge in the student center
cards.notes: Located on the first floor of the Krannert Center, this area provides a safe space for students to study, chat, or relax between classes.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated first-floor lounge in the Krannert Center for quiet study and relaxation.
cards.evidence_claim: Located on the first floor of the Krannert Center, this is a safe space for students to study, chat or just sit around and relax.
cards.access_notes: Open during Krannert Center operating hours; popular with both commuters and residents.

cards.title: The Main-to-Mountain Connector
cards.subtitle: Three-mile paved multi-use path
cards.notes: This paved trail connects the main campus to the mountain campus and remains open even during managed hunts.
cards.short_summary: A three-mile paved path used by students for walking, running, and cycling between campuses.
cards.evidence_claim: The Viking Trail, a three-mile paved trail for walkers, runners, cyclists and rollerbladers, runs between the main campus and the mountain campus.
cards.source_title: Campus Use and Recreation - Berry College
cards.access_notes: Open during daylight hours from the Ladd Center to the mountain campus entrance.

cards.title: On-Campus Camping
cards.subtitle: Student-only tent sites at Victory Lake
cards.notes: Students can reserve one of six tent sites for up to three nights to experience the outdoors without leaving campus.
cards.short_summary: A student-only camping area featuring six tent sites on the banks of Victory Lake.
cards.evidence_claim: The Department of Recreation manages a six site tent camping area on the banks of Victory Lake... The campgrounds are for Berry College students only.
cards.access_notes: Reservations must be submitted 24 hours in advance; gear checkout is available.

cards.title: Art in a Historic General Store
cards.subtitle: Student art exhibitions in Moon Building
cards.notes: Originally the campus general store built by students in 1934, this historic building now houses the art department and gallery.
cards.short_summary: A historic student-built general store repurposed as an art gallery and department space.
cards.evidence_claim: Constructed by students in 1934... formerly Berry's general store and is now our beloved art department.
cards.source_title: Our View: Berry should not tear down Moon
cards.access_notes: Open for student exhibitions and art department activities.

cards.title: The Swan Sanctuary
cards.subtitle: Quiet outdoor spot near the Academy
cards.notes: A favorite for outdoor studying, this lake is home to swans and offers a peaceful environment away from the main academic buildings.
cards.short_summary: A scenic lake on campus known for its resident swans and quiet atmosphere for studying.
cards.evidence_claim: Swan Lake and Berry College are home to swans once again... Swan Lake and the little spot across the street... was always my favorite.
cards.source_title: Swans On The Lake - Berry College
cards.access_notes: Accessible to students and visitors during daylight hours.

cards.title: The Mountain Campus Landmark
cards.subtitle: Stone chapel with stained-glass windows
cards.notes: Built by students in the 1930s, this chapel on the mountain campus is a popular spot for quiet reflection and alumni weddings.
cards.short_summary: A student-built stone chapel on the mountain campus known for its architecture and views.
cards.evidence_claim: Built by Berry students and staff in 1936-37, Frost has become one of the places that visitors to the campus remember.
cards.source_title: Wedding Venue Frost Chapel - Berry College
cards.access_notes: Located on the Mountain Campus; open for visitors and special events.

cards.title: The Elevated Jogging Track
cards.subtitle: Indoor track overlooking the arena
cards.notes: Students use this indoor track for exercise regardless of weather, providing a view of the performance arena and fitness center.
cards.short_summary: An indoor walking and jogging track located within the 131,000-square-foot Cage Center.
cards.evidence_claim: The 131,000-square-foot facility houses... an indoor walk/jog track among its many amenities.
cards.access_notes: Open to students with valid ID; hours vary by day (e.g., 7 a.m. - 9 p.m. Mon-Thu).

cards.title: The Historic Waterwheel
cards.subtitle: Student-built mill with an overshot waterwheel
cards.notes: A landmark for student hikers, this mill features one of the largest overshot waterwheels in the world and is a common stop on the way to the reservoir.
cards.short_summary: A historic mill built by students, featuring a massive waterwheel and serving as a hiking destination.
cards.evidence_claim: Next time, you could start at the Old Mill (which is not far from The House 'O Dreams trail entrance) and hike up to the Berry Reservoir.
cards.access_notes: Accessible via campus roads and trails; popular for photography and hiking.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Discover free social and recreational activities across Berry College's expansive 27,000-acre campus, from historic landmarks to scenic nature trails.

cards.title: Cycle the Viking Trail
cards.subtitle: A 3-mile paved path for students and visitors
cards.notes: Ride or walk this paved 3-mile trail connecting the main campus to the mountain campus. It is open daily during daylight hours for cyclists and joggers.
cards.short_summary: The Viking Trail is a 3-mile paved path connecting Berry's main and mountain campuses for free recreational use.
cards.evidence_claim: The Viking Trail is a three-mile paved trail for walkers, runners, cyclists and rollerbladers, open during daylight hours.
cards.source_title: Campus Use and Recreation - Berry College
cards.access_notes: Open daily during daylight hours; accessible from the Ladd Center.

cards.title: Hike to the House o' Dreams
cards.subtitle: Historic retreat atop Lavender Mountain
cards.notes: Trek the 2.4-mile trail up Lavender Mountain to reach this historic stone cottage. The grounds offer panoramic views and are open to the public for free.
cards.short_summary: The House o' Dreams is a historic stone retreat on Lavender Mountain accessible via a free public hiking trail.
cards.evidence_claim: The trail up the mountain to the house is open to the public and there is no fee to tour the house or the tower.
cards.source_title: Trail Destinations and Heads - Berry College
cards.access_notes: Accessible via the main entrance; visitors must check in at the Welcome Center for a map.

cards.title: Visit the Martha Berry Museum
cards.subtitle: Free admission for the Berry community
cards.notes: Explore exhibits on the college's history and founder Martha Berry. Self-guided tours of the museum building are free for all guests.
cards.short_summary: The Martha Berry Museum offers free self-guided tours detailing the history of the college and its founder.
cards.evidence_claim: A self-guided tour of The Martha Berry Museum is free to all guests.
cards.source_title: Berry College Oak Hill Museum Tours
cards.access_notes: Open Monday through Saturday, 10 a.m. to 5 p.m.

cards.title: Relax by the Ford Reflection Pool
cards.subtitle: Gothic architecture and scenic waters
cards.notes: Visit the iconic Ford Complex to see the English Gothic-style buildings and the large reflection pool, a popular spot for photography and quiet study.
cards.short_summary: The Ford Reflection Pool is a scenic landmark within the Gothic-style Ford Complex, open for public viewing and photography.
cards.evidence_claim: Mirror pools surrounding the building provide beautiful photo backdrops; the site is open for public campus use.
cards.source_title: Ford Buildings at Berry College - Georgia's Rome
cards.access_notes: Visitors must enter through the main gate and present ID at the Welcome Center.

cards.title: Watch the Swans at Swan Lake
cards.subtitle: A peaceful campus wildlife habitat
cards.notes: Walk around Swan Lake to spot the resident trumpeter swans. It is a quiet, scenic area perfect for nature observation and birdwatching.
cards.short_summary: Swan Lake is a campus habitat home to resident swans, offering a free and peaceful nature experience.
cards.evidence_claim: Swan Lake and Berry College are home to swans once again; the area is part of the campus open for public use.
cards.source_title: Swans on the Lake - Berry College
cards.access_notes: Open during daylight hours as part of the main campus grounds.

cards.title: Play the Log Cabin Disc Golf Course
cards.subtitle: 18-hole course on the main campus
cards.notes: Challenge friends to a round on this 18-hole course. Students can check out discs for free from the Cage Center equipment desk.
cards.short_summary: The Log Cabin Disc Golf Course is a free 18-hole facility on campus with equipment available for student checkout.
cards.evidence_claim: Berry College students and faculty/staff can check out discs from the Cage Center; the course is free to play.
cards.access_notes: The first tee is located near the campus chapel; guests must enter through the Visitor's Center.

cards.title: Tee Off at WinShape Course
cards.subtitle: Secondary course near WinShape Centre
cards.notes: Explore the second on-campus disc golf course located behind the WinShape tennis courts. It offers a different terrain for experienced players.
cards.short_summary: The WinShape Disc Golf Course provides a second free 18-hole layout for students and visitors on the mountain campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The WinShape Course 1st Tee is located behind the WinShape Centre Tennis Courts.
cards.access_notes: Located on the mountain campus; open during daylight hours.

cards.title: Spot Deer and Wildlife
cards.subtitle: Nature observation on 27,000 acres
cards.notes: Drive or walk through campus to see the famous deer population. The campus serves as a wildlife refuge with thousands of deer roaming freely.
cards.short_summary: Berry College's vast campus is a wildlife refuge where visitors can observe deer and other animals for free.
cards.evidence_claim: Berry is known for its large numbers of deer; over 15,000 acres fall under the care of the Georgia DNR as a wildlife refuge.
cards.source_title: Campus Use and Recreation - Berry College
cards.access_notes: Best viewed at dawn or dusk; visitors must stay on designated roads and trails.

cards.title: Stroll the Campus Arboretum
cards.subtitle: Educational tree walk on main campus
cards.notes: Follow the self-guided tree walk to learn about the diverse species in the Berry College Arboretum. It is an educational and free outdoor activity.
cards.short_summary: The Berry College Arboretum features a free self-guided tree walk showcasing the campus's diverse botanical collection.
cards.evidence_claim: Berry College established specific trail designations including the Arboretum and Tree Walk.
cards.source_title: Trail Destinations and Heads - Berry College
cards.access_notes: Located on the main campus; maps are available online or at the Welcome Center.

cards.title: Hike the Victory Lake Loop
cards.subtitle: Scenic lakeside trail for students
cards.notes: Walk the loop around Victory Lake for views of the water and surrounding forest. It is a popular spot for student hammocking and relaxation.
cards.short_summary: The Victory Lake Loop is a free hiking trail offering scenic lakeside views and recreational space for students.
cards.evidence_claim: The Department of Recreation manages trails around Victory Lake; it is a popular spot for hiking and relaxing in a hammock.
cards.access_notes: Accessible via the mountain campus; open during daylight hours.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: From the quiet carrels of Memorial Library to collaborative labs in McAllister Hall, Berry College offers diverse environments for focused academic work across its expansive campus.

cards.title: Second Floor Quiet Carrels
cards.subtitle: Memorial Library
cards.notes: Check out a key at the Service Desk for one of 10 individual study carrels. These locked spaces provide a distraction-free zone for deep focus and independent research.
cards.short_summary: Locked individual study rooms on the library's second floor available for two-hour checkouts.
cards.evidence_claim: There are 10 individual study rooms available on the second floor of the library for check-out on a first-come, first-served basis with a 2-hour loan period.
cards.access_notes: Keys must be checked out at the Service Desk; 2-hour limit applies.

cards.title: Collaborative Science Corridors
cards.subtitle: McAllister Hall
cards.notes: Utilize the open and collaborative spaces designed with natural light and intuitive wayfinding. These areas encourage interaction between students and faculty outside traditional labs.
cards.short_summary: Modern collaborative study areas within the 26,500-square-foot Animal Science addition.
cards.evidence_claim: The McAllister Hall Animal Science Building features open and collaborative spaces with an abundance of natural light to encourage hands-on learning.
cards.source_title: Project Profile: Berry College's McAllister Hall Animal Science Building
cards.access_notes: Open during academic building hours; primarily used by science majors.

cards.title: Tech-Forward Collaborative Space
cards.subtitle: Memorial Library
cards.notes: Experiment with new technology in this highly adaptable classroom space. It is designed to foster instruction and enhanced student learning in a collaborative environment.
cards.short_summary: A multi-faceted workspace in the library dedicated to collaborative technology and instruction.
cards.evidence_claim: The Sandbox is a multi-faceted, highly adaptable classroom space dedicated to experimenting with new technology in a collaborative environment.
cards.access_notes: Available during library hours; some sessions may be reserved for classes.

cards.title: The Central Hub Tables
cards.subtitle: Krannert Center
cards.notes: Find a spot at the lobby tables for a social study session. This central hub is ideal for quick reviews between classes or meeting up with student organizations.
cards.short_summary: High-traffic study tables located in the main lobby of the student life center.
cards.evidence_claim: The Krannert Center is the central hub of campus life and features a lobby used for various student activities and informal gatherings.
cards.access_notes: Open during Krannert Center operating hours; can be loud during peak dining times.

cards.title: Humanities Tech Suite
cards.subtitle: Evans Hall Room 206-A
cards.notes: Access general-purpose computing resources in this lab supporting the Evans School of Humanities. It is available for student use during all open building hours.
cards.short_summary: A general access computer lab located in the historic Evans Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: Evans 206-A is a general access facility providing support primarily to the Evans School of Humanities, available during all open hours.
cards.access_notes: Food and drink are strictly prohibited in the computer labs.

cards.title: The Innovation Makerspace
cards.subtitle: Emery Barns Area
cards.notes: Work on interdisciplinary projects in this 7,200-square-foot facility. It provides dedicated design studios and tools for electronics, woodworking, and digital fabrication.
cards.short_summary: A collaborative makerspace for creative technologies and hands-on project development.
cards.evidence_claim: HackBerry Lab is a 7,200-square-foot makerspace that supports students in turning ideas into reality through various design and tech tools.
cards.access_notes: Primarily for Creative Technologies majors, but open to the Berry community for specific projects.

cards.title: Social Study & Snack Zone
cards.subtitle: Memorial Library
cards.notes: Head to the student lounge for a more relaxed atmosphere. You can grab a drink or snack from the nearby bar while working on group assignments.
cards.short_summary: A casual lounge area within the library that allows for socializing and snacking.
cards.evidence_claim: Memorial Library includes a student lounge and a snack bar, providing areas for both individual and group study.
cards.access_notes: Open during regular library hours; snack bar hours may vary.

cards.title: Business School Tech Hub
cards.subtitle: Green Hall
cards.notes: Utilize the computer lab in Green Hall, home to the Campbell School of Business. It is a quiet alternative for students needing specialized business software.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated computer lab for business and economics students in Green Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: Green Hall houses the Campbell School of Business and includes a computer lab for student use.
cards.source_title: Campbell School of Business - Berry College
cards.access_notes: Open during business school hours; priority given to business students.

cards.title: Ford Complex Residential Study
cards.subtitle: East and West Mary Hall
cards.notes: Residents of the Ford Complex can access study rooms located throughout East and West Mary. These provide convenient, late-night study options within the living area.
cards.short_summary: Study rooms located within the historic Mary Hall residence buildings.
cards.evidence_claim: Study rooms are located throughout both East and West Mary Hall in the Ford Complex.
cards.access_notes: Restricted to residents of Mary Hall; available 24/7 for those with card access.

cards.title: The ALC Group Space
cards.subtitle: Memorial Library Room 104
cards.notes: Reserve this space via the EMS system for group projects or collaborative study sessions. It is designed to support active learning and group interaction.
cards.short_summary: A reservable active learning classroom in the library for group study.
cards.evidence_claim: Current Berry students can reserve the ALC - Room 104 in Memorial Library via the EMS system.
cards.access_notes: Requires reservation through the campus EMS system.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Explore the essential streets and corridors surrounding Berry College's massive campus, from the historic downtown Rome districts to the practical shopping hubs of Mount Berry.

cards.title: Historic Downtown Hub
cards.subtitle: Broad Street Corridor
cards.notes: Walk the second-widest Main Street in Georgia to find student favorites like Honeymoon Bakery and Schroeder's New Deli.
cards.short_summary: The primary social and dining corridor of historic downtown Rome.
cards.evidence_claim: Broad Street is listed as a major off-campus hot spot for Berry students, featuring shops and restaurants like Honeymoon Bakery.
cards.access_notes: Public thoroughfare; individual business hours vary.

cards.title: Retail and Dining Anchor
cards.subtitle: Martha Berry Boulevard
cards.notes: Visit this enclosed mall for essentials at Belk or a quick meal at Chick-fil-A, located just south of the main campus gate.
cards.short_summary: A major shopping destination located on the Martha Berry Highway corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: Mount Berry Mall is a primary shopping and dining destination for students on Martha Berry Hwy.
cards.access_notes: Open Monday-Saturday 10am-9pm, Sunday 12pm-6pm.

cards.title: Riverfront Recreation
cards.subtitle: Riverside Parkway
cards.notes: Access the ECO Greenway trail or visit the Rome-Floyd E.C.O. Center to see native wildlife exhibits along the Oostanaula River.
cards.short_summary: A 60-acre park featuring trails, river access, and an environmental education center.
cards.evidence_claim: Ridge Ferry Park on Riverside Parkway houses the E.C.O. Center and serves as a trailhead for the ECO Greenway.
cards.access_notes: Park open daily from dawn to dusk; E.C.O. Center has specific afternoon hours.

cards.title: Casual Dining Corridor
cards.subtitle: Turner McCall Boulevard
cards.notes: Stop by this busy thoroughfare for student-friendly dining options like McAlister's Deli and Krystal.
cards.short_summary: A commercial corridor connecting downtown Rome to the eastern shopping districts.
cards.evidence_claim: Turner McCall Blvd is a key commercial street featuring student-frequented dining like McAlister's Deli.
cards.access_notes: Open daily for lunch and dinner; typically 10:30am-9pm.

cards.title: College Heights Hangout
cards.subtitle: East 2nd Avenue
cards.notes: Grab a New Orleans-style cold brew at PJ's Coffee in the College Heights neighborhood just north of downtown.
cards.short_summary: A neighborhood street in College Heights known for local coffee and residential charm.
cards.evidence_claim: PJ's Coffee is located on East 2nd Ave, serving as a local coffee destination for the community.
cards.access_notes: Open daily; early morning through late afternoon.

cards.title: West Rome Retail Strip
cards.subtitle: Shorter Avenue Corridor
cards.notes: Explore the West Rome area for diverse food options like Provino's Italian Restaurant and various retail centers.
cards.short_summary: A major commercial artery in West Rome near Shorter University.
cards.evidence_claim: Shorter Avenue is a primary commercial corridor in West Rome featuring restaurants like Provino's.
cards.access_notes: Public road; business hours vary.

cards.title: Medical and Dining Loop
cards.subtitle: Redmond Circle
cards.notes: Find quick bites like Bojangles or local favorites like Golden Crown on this loop near the Redmond Regional Medical Center.
cards.short_summary: A circular thoroughfare serving the medical district and local residential areas.
cards.evidence_claim: Redmond Circle features dining options like Bojangles and Golden Crown.
cards.access_notes: Public road; Bojangles open daily from 5am-10pm.

cards.title: Modern Retail Hub
cards.subtitle: Hicks Drive
cards.notes: Shop for dorm decor and supplies at Five Below or other retailers in this newer shopping development.
cards.short_summary: A contemporary retail center located off the East Rome Bypass.
cards.evidence_claim: Hicks Drive is home to the East Bend shopping center, featuring retailers like Five Below.
cards.access_notes: Retail hours typically 10am-9pm.

cards.title: River District Dining
cards.subtitle: West 3rd Street
cards.notes: Experience the growing River District with upscale dining at Aventine, located near the confluence of Rome's rivers.
cards.short_summary: A key street in the developing River District of downtown Rome.
cards.evidence_claim: Aventine is a prominent restaurant located on West 3rd Street in the River District.
cards.access_notes: Dinner service Tuesday-Saturday; reservations recommended.

cards.title: Riverboat and History
cards.subtitle: Heritage Park Road
cards.notes: See the Roman Holiday riverboat or explore the trails where the Etowah and Oostanaula rivers meet to form the Coosa.
cards.short_summary: A historic park at the confluence of Rome's three rivers.
cards.evidence_claim: Heritage Park on Heritage Park Road is the docking site for the Roman Holiday riverboat.
cards.access_notes: Open daily from dawn to dusk.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Discover the unique rituals and long-standing traditions of Berry College, from the massive Mountain Day celebration to the daily presence of a vast deer population on the world's largest campus.

cards.title: The Grand March
cards.subtitle: A Centennial Birthday Celebration
cards.notes: Join thousands on Lavender Mountain for a choreographed march in class-specific colors. Seniors wear blue or white while underclassmen wear pink or blue to honor historical uniforms.
cards.short_summary: The Grand March is the centerpiece of Mountain Day, where students march in formation to celebrate founder Martha Berry's birthday.
cards.evidence_claim: The Grand March involves students lining up by class and wearing specific colors as an homage to old Berry uniforms, a tradition dating back over 100 years.
cards.source_title: Berry College Mountain Day Student Information
cards.access_notes: Held annually in October on the Mountain Campus; open to students, alumni, and families.

cards.title: The Penny Drop
cards.subtitle: Donating Your Age for Scholarships
cards.notes: Carry pennies equal to your age and drop them into a basket at the base of the hill during the Grand March. The collection supports the Save A Student Scholarship fund.
cards.short_summary: Students drop pennies corresponding to their age into a basket during the Mountain Day march to support student scholarships.
cards.evidence_claim: Students participating in the Grand March have pennies equal to their age ready to drop in the basket at the base of the hill to support Berry scholarships.
cards.access_notes: Occurs during the Saturday Grand March on Mountain Campus.

cards.title: Marthapalooza
cards.subtitle: Late-Night Carnival in the Clara Bowl
cards.notes: Enjoy carnival rides, food booths, and live bands from 10 PM to 2 AM. This late-night celebration follows the Mountain Day festivities and is free for students with ID.
cards.short_summary: Marthapalooza is a massive late-night carnival held on the Saturday of Mountain Day weekend featuring rides and games.
cards.evidence_claim: Marthapalooza takes place from 10pm until 2am on the main campus and includes carnival rides, booths, games, and food.
cards.source_title: Berry College Mountain Day Parent Information
cards.access_notes: Held Saturday night of Mountain Day weekend; free for students with a wristband.

cards.title: Mountain Day Olympics
cards.subtitle: Dorm vs. Dorm Field Day
cards.notes: Compete in classic field day events like the egg toss and tug-o-war on Evans Lawn. Residence halls and commuter teams vie for the title of Olympic Champions.
cards.short_summary: The Mountain Day Olympics is a spirited field day competition between student housing communities held every October.
cards.evidence_claim: Mountain Day Olympics are held on Evans Lawn where residence halls, commuters, faculty and staff compete in field day-type events.
cards.source_title: Mountain Day Olympics - Berry College Events
cards.access_notes: Typically held on the Friday afternoon of Mountain Day weekend on Evans Lawn.

cards.title: Living with the Deer
cards.subtitle: The 1:3 Student-to-Deer Ratio
cards.notes: Observe the thousands of white-tailed deer that roam the 27,000-acre campus. They are so common that they are considered unofficial mascots and frequent the academic quads.
cards.short_summary: Berry College is famous for its massive resident deer population, which outnumbers the students on campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Berry is a large, outdoorsy campus with a student to deer ratio of approximately 1:3, with estimates of 1,500 to 2,500 deer.
cards.source_title: Berry College Review by Anna - Appily
cards.access_notes: Visible throughout the campus at all times, especially near the Ford Complex and wooded trails.

cards.title: The Gate of Opportunity
cards.subtitle: Enter to Learn, Leave to Serve
cards.notes: Walk through the historic white gate that served as the original main entrance. It symbolizes Martha Berry's mission for students to work for their education.
cards.short_summary: The Gate of Opportunity is a symbolic landmark representing the college's historical commitment to accessible education through work.
cards.evidence_claim: Martha Berry named the main entrance 'The Gate of Opportunity,' where students entered to learn and left to serve.
cards.access_notes: Located on the main campus drive; accessible for photos and walking.

cards.title: The Viking Battleaxe
cards.subtitle: Leading the Team to Valhalla
cards.notes: Watch the football team march to Valhalla Stadium led by a player carrying a massive two-sided battleaxe. This totem serves as the team's battle flag and mascot.
cards.short_summary: The Viking Battleaxe is a modern tradition where the football team is led onto the field by a ceremonial axe.
cards.evidence_claim: An enormous two-sided battleaxe serves as a totem and battle flag, leading the team as it marches to the stadium, known as Valhalla.
cards.access_notes: Visible during the pre-game march at home football games at Valhalla Stadium.

cards.title: Eco-Friendly Mowers
cards.subtitle: Sheep for Kudzu Control
cards.notes: Spot the campus sheep herd used for sustainable landscaping. These animals help control invasive kudzu and are a common sight for students working on the grounds crew.
cards.short_summary: Berry College uses a resident sheep herd as a sustainable method for controlling invasive plant species on its vast acreage.
cards.evidence_claim: The university uses sheep to control kudzu rather than chemical herbicides, a practice documented in campus sustainability reports.
cards.access_notes: Sheep are moved to different grazing areas; often seen near the animal science units or Lavender Mountain.

cards.title: The Ford Catacombs
cards.subtitle: Underground Tunnels of the Castle
cards.notes: Learn about the 'catacombs'—a series of utility tunnels beneath the Gothic Ford Buildings. While mostly for HVAC, they are a staple of campus lore and ghost stories.
cards.short_summary: The Ford Catacombs are a network of underground tunnels beneath the college's iconic Gothic architecture.
cards.evidence_claim: There are a series of closed tunnels running underneath the Ford buildings, known on campus as the 'catacombs,' primarily housing air conditioning ductwork.
cards.source_title: Hollywood at Berry College? Stranger Things Have Happened
cards.access_notes: Tunnels are closed to the public for safety, but the Ford Buildings above are accessible.

cards.title: The Old Mill
cards.subtitle: Student-Built Engineering Marvel
cards.notes: Visit the 42-foot overshot waterwheel built by students in 1930. It remains one of the most photographed spots on campus and a symbol of the 'Head, Heart, and Hands' philosophy.
cards.short_summary: The Old Mill is a historic, student-constructed landmark featuring one of the largest overshot waterwheels in the world.
cards.evidence_claim: The Old Mill was built in 1930 by students and features an overshot wheel that is 42 feet in diameter.
cards.access_notes: Located on the Mountain Campus; open to visitors from dawn to dusk.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at Berry College, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A guide to the essential orientation activities and campus landmarks for new students during Viking Venture weekend at Berry College.

cards.title: Wednesday Move-In
cards.subtitle: Start of Viking Venture
cards.notes: Arrive on Wednesday to move into your residence hall and meet your RAs. This marks the official start of your transition into the Berry community.
cards.short_summary: New students move into campus housing on the Wednesday before classes begin.
cards.evidence_claim: Incoming residential students move into their residence hall room on the Wednesday prior to classes beginning and participate in Viking Venture activities.
cards.access_notes: Required for all new first-year and transfer students taking BCC 100/200.

cards.title: First BCC 100 Session
cards.subtitle: Academic Introduction
cards.notes: Meet your academic advisor and classmates for your first BCC 100 session. You will discuss the common book and learn about the Berry Journey.
cards.short_summary: The first academic meeting for new students to discuss the orientation book.
cards.evidence_claim: Activities include getting to know your classmates and academic advisor during your first BCC 100/200 class and book discussion.
cards.access_notes: Mandatory academic session during orientation week.

cards.title: LifeWorks Orientation
cards.subtitle: Student Work Program
cards.notes: Meet your work supervisor and learn about Berry's unique student work program, which provides professional experience for all students.
cards.short_summary: Orientation for Berry's premier student work program, LifeWorks.
cards.evidence_claim: New students meet their work supervisor during LifeWorks Orientation as part of Viking Venture.
cards.access_notes: Required for students participating in the campus work program.

cards.title: Be Berry Program
cards.subtitle: Culture of Belonging
cards.notes: Participate in this program to reflect on your values and learn how to contribute to a culture of belonging at Berry College.
cards.short_summary: A values-based orientation program for new students.
cards.evidence_claim: The 'Be Berry' Program involves reflecting on values and contributing to a culture of belonging at Berry.
cards.access_notes: Held in the Krannert Center or designated campus venues.

cards.title: Rage in the Cage
cards.subtitle: Late Night Social
cards.notes: Join this high-energy social event at the athletic center. It is a staple of the first weekend for meeting other new students.
cards.short_summary: A popular late-night social event held at the Cage Center during orientation.
cards.evidence_claim: Optional activities during Viking Venture include 'Rage in the Cage' at the athletic center.
cards.access_notes: Late-night event typically held on Friday or Saturday of orientation.

cards.title: Club Krannert
cards.subtitle: Student Center Party
cards.notes: Explore the student center during this themed event featuring music and activities hosted by the Krannert Center Activities Board.
cards.short_summary: A social event hosted in the Krannert Center for new students.
cards.evidence_claim: Viking Venture includes optional activities like 'Club Krannert' for students to explore campus.
cards.access_notes: Evening social event open to all new students.

cards.title: Tour the Ford Castles
cards.subtitle: Iconic Architecture
cards.notes: Walk through the English Gothic-style Ford Complex. These 'castles' are among the most photographed spots on the world's largest campus.
cards.short_summary: The iconic English Gothic buildings donated by Henry Ford.
cards.evidence_claim: The Ford Complex is described as Berry's iconic castles and is a primary spot for student-led campus tours.
cards.access_notes: Open for walking tours; interior access may vary by building.

cards.title: Visit the Old Mill
cards.subtitle: Historic Landmark
cards.notes: Check out the historic waterwheel at the Old Mill. It is a peaceful spot perfect for a first-weekend photo with new friends.
cards.short_summary: A historic mill featuring one of the world's largest overshot waterwheels.
cards.evidence_claim: The Old Mill is a picturesque campus landmark that visitors and students are encouraged to visit for photos.
cards.source_title: Old Mill at Berry College - Georgia's Rome
cards.access_notes: Free entry; requires campus gate check-in with a valid ID.

cards.title: Hike to House o' Dreams
cards.subtitle: Mountain Viewpoint
cards.notes: Hike up Lavender Mountain to Martha Berry's historic retreat. The 4.8-mile round trip offers views of the campus and Rome, Georgia.
cards.short_summary: A scenic hike to the historic stone cottage atop Lavender Mountain.
cards.evidence_claim: The House o' Dreams trail is a 4.8-mile out-and-back hike located at Berry College, open to the public and students.
cards.access_notes: Trails are open during daylight hours; check for seasonal hunt closures.

cards.title: Evening at Valhalla
cards.subtitle: Viking Athletics
cards.notes: Visit the home of the Vikings for a weekend athletic event or a sunset view from the stands of this 2,500-seat stadium.
cards.short_summary: Berry's primary stadium for football, track and field, and lacrosse.
cards.evidence_claim: Valhalla Stadium serves as a gathering place for students and fans for football and other athletic events.
cards.access_notes: Open for scheduled athletic events and orientation gatherings.
